title: Introduction to Code Sandbox and the Structure of the Module
summary: Introduces CodeSandbox as the browser-based editor used for the React module, explains why it replaces local VS Code here, and outlines the learn-then-practice rhythm of the lessons.

concepts.heading: What CodeSandbox offers
points: Browser-based development environment with instant hosting: every project gets a shareable URL for friends, colleagues or a portfolio.
Designed with React in mind: no manual React install, built-in npm dependency management, and live collaboration.
Free to use. Sign-up (via the link in the course resources) works with GitHub, Google or Apple accounts.

concepts.heading: Why not local VS Code for this module
points: React releases change details frequently and the course cannot be re-recorded each time, so a shared environment keeps everyone on identical React versions and avoids deprecation surprises.
Provided starter and final sandboxes mean everyone sees the same code and tooling, so learning focuses on fundamentals (components, hooks, functional style) instead of setup problems.
Local development is still possible; the next lesson is a text guide for it, but it is not recommended until the basics are solid. Docs cover any later version changes.

concepts.heading: Module structure
points: Pattern: a lesson teaches one skill in a demo sandbox, then a separate practice sandbox lets the learner apply it.
After enough skills are built, the Keeper app project is introduced in several parts, each applying earlier skills.

task.name: Create a CodeSandbox account

steps: Open the CodeSandbox link from the course resources.
Choose GitHub, Google or Apple to register.

pitfalls: (Extra) CodeSandbox's UI and templates change over time, and the reference repo uses local Vite projects instead, so sandbox links may differ from what the repo shows.
